message: And Clancy, I guess the class-as-educational-preparedness phenomenon I mentioned ties in very much to your question, and I'm afraid I have no answer. (No surprise there, right?) In some ways, the situation seems to involve conflicting ideals over how democratic education should work: should instruction be the ladder that gives all students an equal amount of rungs to see over the economic fence, so that those who are taller maintain their natural advantage (I know, lousy metaphor), or should it be the rising tide that lifts all boats *to the same level*? Do you give every student the same thing, or make sure every student gets to the same point?
